meta.one_idea: A function handed a list works on that same list, so += inside changes yours. Python's ready-made functions min, max, sum and sorted give back a new answer and leave your list alone.
outcomes: Predict what a list prints after a function changes it with +=.
Explain why list_x = list_x + [3] inside a function leaves the caller's list unchanged.
Predict the output when a function with a list default is called three times.
Use min and max on separate values, on a list, and on strings.
Use sum on a list, and say why sum(3, 5, 4) fails.
Use sorted, with and without reverse=True, and say that the old list is unchanged.
Write a program that collects the digits of a string and prints their sum, smallest and largest.

Words: a variable points at a list. Two names can point at one list. Never say reference or object on screen; the deck's word mutable is said once, on C1, as: a list can change in place.

beats.name: One default list for every call

cards.title: One default list
cards.purpose: A default list is made once, when the def runs. Every call that leaves list_x out points at that same list, so the third call finds the 3 from the first. Watch the default list sit there between calls.
cards.heading: A list as a default value
show: The default list is made once, when the def runs. Not every time the function is called.

code.src:
def add_item(list_x=[]):
    list_x += [3]
    print(list_x)

add_item()
add_item([1,2])
add_item()

presses.screen: add_item_default.py with line numbers (deck slide 16), an empty output box, and an empty space for lists. Caption: <q>What does line 7 print?</q> Options: A <q>[3]</q>, B <q>[3, 3]</q>, C <q>[]</q>, D <q>[1, 2, 3, 3]</q>.
presses.say: Last class: a default fills what we leave out. Option A, hands up. B. C. D.

presses.screen: One step per press, following data.steps, caption from the data. Press 1 of the walk: the def runs and the default list appears beside it, empty. Then each call: list_x's arrow, the change, the print, and the call ending.
presses.say: Before each call: which list will list_x point at?

presses.screen: The output box holds <q>[3]</q>, <q>[1, 2, 3]</q>, <q>[3, 3]</q>. The default list, holding [3, 3], is ringed. Caption: <q>The default list is made once, when the def runs. Not every time the function is called.</q>
presses.say: Made once, when the def ran. Who voted B? The 3 from line 5 was still there.

must: A variable is a name tag with an arrow to a list. Two arrows can point at one list. A list that no arrow points at vanishes at once: no grey ghost. A function's default list sits beside its def, from the press the def runs, and stays there.
A call opens the function's own area beside its block. Its names (list_x) live there and vanish when the call ends. The lists they point at sit in one shared place, outside both areas.
The default list appears on the def press, before any call, and never leaves the screen.
The list [1, 2] from line 6 vanishes when that call ends. The default list does not.
Output lines stay in the box as the walk goes on. They are the finding.
One step per press.
must_not: Show a free code box, a picker or an input field. It runs this one program.
Draw the default list inside the call's area. It belongs to the def.

steps.caption: Line 1: the def runs. The default list is made now, once: [].
Line 5: add_item(). list_x points at the default list. It holds [].
Line 2: list_x += [3]. The list is now [3].
Line 3: print(list_x). It prints [3].
The call ends. list_x goes. The default list stays. It still holds [3].
Line 6: add_item([1,2]). list_x points at a new list [1, 2].
Line 2: list_x += [3]. The list is now [1, 2, 3].
Line 3: print(list_x). It prints [1, 2, 3].
The call ends. list_x goes. The default list stays. It still holds [3]. No name points at [1, 2, 3] now, so it goes too.
Line 7: add_item(). list_x points at the default list. It holds [3].
Line 2: list_x += [3]. The list is now [3, 3].
Line 3: print(list_x). It prints [3, 3].
The call ends. list_x goes. The default list stays. It still holds [3, 3].
